//: Project-specific rules for the agent queue. Any key you leave out falls back to the built-in default. AGENT_QUEUE_* environment variables override this file. Keys starting with // are comments and are ignored. Full reference: the plugin README, section 'Configuration'. Ready-made examples: templates/examples/ in the plugin.
//projectName: Project name (init fills it in). Task prompts tell agents to read, at the top of each skill's SKILL.md, the section that applies the skill to this project.
//cliHint: How the queue CLI is spelled in prompts, reports and the INBOX.
//risk: moneyKeywords: substrings (case-insensitive) of a task's paths or title that mean it TOUCHES MONEY -> high risk, and the task waits for human approval before it starts, e.g. ["payment", "invoice"]. migrationPaths: substrings of a path that mean a DB schema/migration change -> high risk, gated the same way, e.g. ["db/migrations/"]. highPatterns / mediumPatterns: case-insensitive regexes on the task's `touches` -> high risk adds QA + security, medium adds QA.
//skills: Each entry: {skill, domain, globs, roots, reminder}. `globs`: the PreToolUse hook injects `reminder` whenever a matching file is edited. `roots`: path prefixes also matched in the task's `File:` line and verify commands (e.g. `cd services/api && ...`) so the prompt names the skill before any file is touched. The skill must exist at .claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md. `domain` feeds pattern selection (two domains -> Router).
//locks: Exclusive locks: name -> globs. A task whose `touches` hit a lock runs in the SERIAL lane, one at a time. A built-in `lockfile` lock (package.json and npm/yarn/pnpm lockfiles) always exists. A glob starting with ! excludes paths. Example: {"db-schema": ["db/migrations/**"]}.
//testDb: A verify command containing one of `commands` needs a test database whose URL is in the variable `envVar`; `envFile` is a .env file that may define it. If it is missing, the command is reported as skipped (not failed) and the task goes to needs-human instead of done. Each parallel worker gets its own Postgres schema (agent_w<n>) through `options=-c search_path=...`; set `schemaParam` to true if your migration tool also needs `schema=...` in the URL (e.g. Prisma).
//commit: One commit per finished task. The conventional-commit type is the first key of `typeKeywords` (in order) whose keywords appear in the task title or scope (lower-case substring match); no match = chore. Declaring `typeKeywords` replaces the whole table - add words in your backlog's language if it is not English. `trailers` are appended to every commit message ([] = none).
//diffIgnore: Globs NOT counted toward the line/file thresholds when `pattern` measures a diff (tests, docs, generated files). They still count for the 'edited a file outside touches' check. Declaring this key replaces the whole list - keep the defaults you still want.
//worker: Git-ignored dependency directories shared with each parallel worker's worktree, so nothing is reinstalled. linkDirs are SYMLINKED; cloneDirs are COPIED (copy-on-write where the filesystem supports it) for tools that refuse symlinks pointing outside the project. A path may not be in both lists. Monorepos list every one, e.g. ["node_modules", "packages/api/node_modules"]. Write `node_modules` without a trailing slash in .gitignore so the symlink does not show up in git status.
//workers: Number of parallel workers (each with its own worktree, test-DB schema and e2e ports). Size it to your machine's RAM. AGENT_QUEUE_WORKERS overrides it.
//resources: COUNTABLE shared resources: limit how many tasks hold one at the same time, without forcing the serial lane (unlike `locks`). A task holds a resource when one of its verify commands matches a regex in `verify`. Add "serial": true to also run those tasks in the serial lane. Example, one browser e2e stack at a time: {"e2e-stack": {"verify": ["playwright"], "limit": 1}}.
//roles: Orchestration roles, merged with the four built-in ones (developer, qa, security, planner). Each role: {kind: developer|evaluator|reviewer|fixer|planner, when: {domains?, riskAtLeast?, touches?, locks?, openBugs?, always?, diff?}, skills: [..], writes: [globs], model: opus|sonnet|haiku, bash?: ["Bash(npx vitest:*)"], modelByRound?: [{from: 2, model: "opus"}], maxBudgetUsd?: number}. The `when` keys are ORed; `diff` ({paths, added?}, reviewers only) is an extra check on the real diff. Each role needs a prompt file .claude/agents/<role>.md - start reviewers from the plugin's templates/agent-reviewer.md. Example: {"docs-reviewer": {"kind": "reviewer", "when": {"touches": ["docs/**"]}, "writes": [], "model": "haiku"}}.
//headings: Markdown headings that are part of the task/bug/question FILE FORMAT - the harness reads and writes them. Change them only if your backlog already uses other words (e.g. another language), and then change tasks/_templates/ to match. `answer` is also the `Answer:` line in the INBOX; `criticalPath` is the phrase that marks the critical-path line in tasks/INDEX.md; `bugSections` are the 8 required bug sections in order (the last one is the repro test).
//ci: CI workflow to watch with the GitHub CLI (`gh`): {"workflow": "CI", "branch": "main", "gate": "warn", "localHint": "make ci-<job>"}. localHint (optional) = command shown as-is in the INBOX for rerunning a red job locally; write `<job>` where the job name goes. warn = report a red CI in the INBOX and conductor output; block = additionally stop pushing and stop starting new work while that branch is red. null = off (no `gh` calls).
//dashboard: Read-only dashboard (listens on 127.0.0.1 only). port: default port (--port N overrides). tokenWarnPerTask: tokens (integer > 0) on ONE task above which the dashboard highlights it; null = never.
